body.name: Fixed-query conditional-kernel class
body.construction:
Let
\[
 \mathcal Z_{\delta_0}
 =\left\{z=(z_1^\top,\ldots,z_S^\top)^\top\in([0,1]^d)^S:
 \min_{1\le s\le S}\operatorname{dist}(z_s,\partial[0,1]^d)
 \ge\delta_0\right\}.
\]
For each fixed \(z_0\in\mathcal Z_{\delta_0}\), define
\(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) to be the class of labelled conditional
kernels \(\xi=(\mathbb K_\xi;\mu,m,\Sigma)\) for the observed array
\[
 \bigl((B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}})_{s,i},(X_{st})_{s,t},
       (Q_{sti})_{s,t,i},(Z_j)_{j=1}^{N}\bigr)
\]
at the fixed query \(z_0\).  The label satisfies
\(\mu_s=\mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\),
\(m_s(x)=\mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[Q_{sti}\mid X_{st}=x]\), and
\(\Sigma=\operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb K_\xi}(Z_j)\).  The kernel, with the
query adjoined as the constant \(z_0\), must satisfy pointwise at this query
all member properties listed in \texttt{def:panel-model-class}.  In
particular: \(|B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}|\vee|Q_{sti}|\le B\); every
\(m_s\in\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\); every \(X_{st}\) has a density
\(f_{st\mid z_0}\) satisfying \(c_X\le f_{st\mid z_0}(x)\le C_X\) for
Lebesgue-almost-every \(x\), uniformly in \(s,t\); the design sequence of
each cohort has \(\beta_s(k\mid z_0)\le\beta_0\rho_0^k\).  With
\(\mathcal X=\sigma((X_{st})_{s,t})\), conditional on \(\mathcal X\) the
unit histories are independent across \((s,i)\) and obey
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[Q_{sti}\mid\mathcal X]=m_s(X_{st}),
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X]=\mu_s;
\]
and the donor sample is independent of the complete joint panel, is i.i.d.,
and obeys
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}Z_j=z_0,
 \qquad c_\Sigma I_{Sd}\preceq\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_{Sd},
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 \|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)\|_2^4\le B^4.
\]
The historical paths are observed exactly.  Membership also requires an
extension by the potential wealth and return variables obeying consistency,
event-date transport, bounded wealth, and \texttt{def:buyhold-level}; this
makes every causal regular conditional kernel a member while leaving the
statistical functional below distinct from the causal target.  Expectations
and probabilities indexed by \(\xi\) are taken under \(\mathbb K_\xi\).
